subject.title: Multi-tenant hosting: openclaw fleet cell supervisor MVP (per-tenant isolated instances)

question: Should OpenClaw core own the privileged lifecycle supervisor for per-tenant containers, or provide a hardened cell contract for established external orchestration?
rationale: Both approaches preserve the documented one-trust-domain-per-gateway model, but they create materially different long-term security, upgrade, storage, and operator-support obligations that repository behavior cannot decide automatically.

options.title: External orchestrator contract
options.body: Document and validate hardened cells while adding only narrow OpenClaw health, token, state, and upgrade interfaces that existing container tools lack.

options.title: Core fleet supervisor
options.body: Sponsor a bounded MVP with an explicit threat model, shared-state SQLite registry, lifecycle API, and tested upgrade and recovery guarantees.

recommendation.title: External orchestrator contract
recommendation.body: Document and validate hardened cells while adding only narrow OpenClaw health, token, state, and upgrade interfaces that existing container tools lack.

likelyOwner.reason: The current trust-model guidance and recent gateway/container lifecycle hardening make this the strongest history-backed decision-routing candidate.
